title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Küttler, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Tim Rocktäschel, Sebastian Riedel, Douwe Kiela
why_trusted: The paper that introduced and named retrieval-augmented generation, from Facebook AI Research, published in the NeurIPS 2020 proceedings and cited more than 6,000 times.

evidence.venue: NeurIPS 2020 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33)

title: Introducing Contextual Retrieval
authors: Anthropic engineering team (research and writing by Daniel Ford)
why_trusted: Written by the Anthropic team that created Contextual Retrieval, on Anthropic's own site; it is the primary description of the technique and reports measured retrieval failure rates for embeddings, BM25, and reranking.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Vladimir Karpukhin, Barlas Oguz, Sewon Min, Patrick Lewis, Ledell Wu, Sergey Edunov, Danqi Chen, Wen-tau Yih
why_trusted: The EMNLP 2020 paper that showed retrieval with learned dense embeddings beats keyword search for question answering; it is the retriever used inside the original RAG model and is cited more than 5,000 times.

title: AI Engineering
why_trusted: The O'Reilly Media book (2025) that the AI engineering playbook names as the primary text of the field; it has a chapter on RAG and agents. The book is paid, so the link goes to the author's free companion repository.

title: Optimizing LLM Accuracy
why_trusted: The official OpenAI developer guide on choosing between prompting, RAG, and fine-tuning, on OpenAI's own documentation domain; a major model provider explaining a general decision it did not invent.

title: Introduction to RAG
why_trusted: The official developer documentation of LlamaIndex, a major open-source RAG framework, on the project's own domain (the homepage listed by its GitHub repository); it explains the general concept of RAG and its five stages, which LlamaIndex did not create.
